name: Sanctions & coercion
summary: EU sanctioned 113 Russian-linked targets incl. 49 banks on 16 Nov; a 22nd package is due before the 26–27 Nov summit
state: On 16 Nov the EU listed 12 individuals and 101 entities linked to Russia's war economy, including 47 commercial banks, two other credit institutions, 27 oil, gas and mining firms and 15 companies tied to shadow-fleet tankers (Ukrainska Pravda). EU foreign policy chief Kallas said on 16 Nov a 22nd package would be presented within days, with approval targeted by Christmas (UNN). No major economy cut off from payment systems or large seizure of sovereign assets was found as of 19 Nov, so Watch holds.
for_you: Firms trading with Russia, or handling Russian-linked shipping, banking or energy, face wider compliance checks as EU lists grow. UK businesses can check current designations through the OFSI consolidated list.
rubric_hit: Watch: major new EU package (113 listings incl. 49 banks, 16 Nov); no payment-system cut-off or sovereign asset seizure (Alert line)

sources.title: Ukrainska Pravda — EU imposes sweeping sanctions on Russian banks, shadow fleet and e-commerce

why: Sanctions are now a frontline weapon; secondary sanctions and asset seizures fragment global finance and trade.
